**SHOCKING DRAFT PICK ROCKS SPORTS WORLD: CHRIS SUMMERS SELECTED BY CLEVELAND CAVALIERS**

In a stunning move that has left fans and analysts alike scratching their heads, the Cleveland Cavaliers, a team typically associated with the hardwood of the National Basketball Association, has drafted Chris Summers, a 27-year-old American ice hockey player. The news broke late last night, sending shockwaves throughout the sports world. Summers, a defenseman who has played for the Arizona Coyotes and New York Rangers in the National Hockey League, was taken 25th overall in the second round of the NBA draft. "I'm still in disbelief," Summers said in an exclusive interview with our publication. "I mean, I've always loved basketball, but I never thought I'd be drafted by an NBA team. It's an incredible opportunity, and I'm excited to see where it takes me." When asked about the transition from ice to hardwood, Summers acknowledged it wouldn't be easy. "It's going to be a challenge, no question. But I'm a competitor, and I'm willing to put in the work to learn the game and contribute to the team." Cavaliers General Manager, Koby Altman, defended the unconventional pick, citing Summers' athleticism and competitive drive. "We're always looking for ways to shake things up and bring a new perspective to the game. Chris brings a unique set of skills and a winning mentality that we believe can translate to the basketball court." Altman pointed to Summers' impressive stats in the NHL, including a plus-12 rating and 12 points in 42 games last season. "He's a winner, and we think he can bring that same level of success to our organization." Not everyone is convinced, however. NBA analyst, Mark Jackson, was critical of the pick, calling it a "publicity stunt" and questioning the Cavaliers' commitment to building a competitive team. "I just don't see how a hockey player, no matter how athletic, can make an impact in the NBA," Jackson said. "It's a different game, with different skills and strategies. I think the Cavs are taking a huge risk here." Despite the criticism, Summers remains optimistic about his chances. "I'm not here to prove anyone wrong or right. I'm here to work hard, learn the game, and help the Cavaliers win. That's all that matters to me."
